resources.scope: GPU cost is the assigned single worker process interval. Queue waiting is excluded. Episode and model-attempt wall intervals are different nested operational measures and must not be added to worker GPU seconds. Memory peaks are maxima of recorded samples, not exact allocator peaks; no per-slot GPU kernel-time measurement exists.

checks: Each settled call has started=true, exact reported prompt+completion=total=charge, and matches same-member same-call same-response material summary.
701 material decisions bijectively match 701 settled ledger calls; 9 pre-generation admission rejections have no charge and no invented model tokens.
Each slot sums call charges to its sealed ledger and has held_tokens=0; all slots conserve charged+available=500000.

Per-member material totals and 16 original slots match sealed training-material-binding; fixed actor denominator=16*2*that slot/member own output tokens; critic denominator=16*2*that slot/member actual generated decision count. The 9 pre-generation rejections are preserved as original decision opportunities, not invented token or critic targets.

denominator_formula.actor: 16 original joint slots * 2 active members * all own output tokens of this slot/member
denominator_formula.critic: 16 original joint slots * 2 active members * all own actual generated decisions of this slot/member (the 9 pre-generation budget refusals have no model output target)

training_material.scope: Static admission of original per-member selected-input and sampled own-output tokens only. All 16*2 base masks remain true, including five successful-unmapped joint slots and one non-submission R=0 slot. This does not claim 9B probability/backward qualification, update throughput or learning benefit.

common_and_guards.common_rng_digest_schema: tensor_tree_digest({rng_cpu: CPU RNG tensor, rng_cuda: list of CUDA RNG tensors})
common_and_guards.guard_rng_digest_schema: tensor_tree_digest({cpu: CPU RNG tensor, cuda: list of CUDA RNG tensors}); keys differ from the common digest schema, so cross-schema hashes must not be compared directly.

collection_guard.scope: Only Torch CPU/CUDA RNG is restored. Probe window IDs, logs and generation/cache counters remain real; learner tensors and steps are never rolled back.

source_contract.contract:
# Build a SQL script inventory from the real parser

Deliver reader.statement_records(script) and report.summarize(script).
The script is empty/whitespace or a sequence of valid, flat single-table SELECT,
UPDATE and DELETE statements. SELECT projects one column or one literal; UPDATE
sets one column to a constant; an optional WHERE compares one column with one
constant. Identifiers contain ASCII letters, digits and underscores and start
with a letter. Constants are nonnegative integers or single-quoted ASCII text
without escaped quotes; text may contain spaces or semicolons. Statement keywords
may be upper/lowercase. Spaces and newlines separate tokens/statements. There
are no comments, joins, nested queries, functions, transactions or invalid SQL
acceptance cases. Statements may repeat; the last semicolon is optional.

reader.statement_records uses real sqlparse.split and sqlparse.parse, then each
parsed Statement.get_type(). Return [{"text": split_piece, "kind": kind}, ...]
in script order. split_piece is exactly the text produced by sqlparse.split
(including its retained statement semicolon and internal spelling/whitespace);
kind is SELECT, UPDATE or DELETE from the real Statement API. Do not replace
the parser with string splitting or a second parser. Empty input returns [].

report.summarize consumes reader.statement_records and returns exactly
{"statements": records, "counts": {"SELECT": n, "UPDATE": n, "DELETE": n},
 "total": number_of_records}. Keep the same records/order and duplicates. Counts
and total are integers; include all three count keys even when zero. Empty input
has empty statements, all counts zero, and total zero. Preserve caller input.

For example, "SELECT label FROM bins; UPDATE bins SET flag = 1;" produces two
records with kinds SELECT/UPDATE, counts 1/1/0, and total 2. A semicolon inside
a quoted literal is not a statement boundary.

# Work and acceptance

This is one immutable root goal, not an execution task list. Two equal members
start with private copies and no assigned tasks or owners. Create, revise, claim
and coordinate your own work as useful. One member may complete everything;
communication, two-person editing and a particular work order are not required.

Only the declared application modules and test_member.py are editable. The real
pinned library, contract, public checks and supplied grammar assets are read-only.
Public checks cover the declared semantics plus a bounded original upstream
regression subset. Private acceptance uses different inputs under the same
contract. No behavior outside the declared legal input domain is assessed.
Use the stated real API and reusable product: calling a dummy API and ignoring
its result does not implement the contract. Preserve caller inputs including
JSON scalar types. Output types are exact; floats and booleans do not substitute
for required integers. A current tested fixed submission is needed, but saving
a submission is not independent acceptance. There is no CLI, network, persistent
service or external producer to build.

args:
SELECT label FROM bins;
UPDATE bins SET flag = 1;
select 'a;b' FROM logs; DELETE FROM logs WHERE id = 2; select 'a;b' FROM logs;

UPDATE events SET note = 'x;y';
SELECT 'plain' FROM events
update boxes SET value = 4; SELECT code FROM boxes WHERE id = 3; delete FROM boxes; SELECT code FROM boxes WHERE id = 3;

UPDATE events SET note = 'x;y';
SELECT 'plain' FROM events

source_contract.upstream_test_body:
def test_statement_get_type():
    def f(sql):
        return sqlparse.parse(sql)[0]

    assert f('select * from foo').get_type() == 'SELECT'
    assert f('update foo').get_type() == 'UPDATE'
    assert f(' update foo').get_type() == 'UPDATE'
    assert f('\nupdate foo').get_type() == 'UPDATE'
    assert f('foo').get_type() == 'UNKNOWN'
source_contract.upstream_subset_scope: One original fixture-free test function, five direct library assertions. Its UNKNOWN input is a library regression, not an extra application-domain acceptance requirement. The full upstream suite was not run.
source_contract.finite_coverage_limit: The same three public semantic invocations, one upstream test and three task-private invocations are repeated for 15 final versions; aggregate 105/105 is not 105 different task cases. Six application invocations use five distinct SQL input strings, and neither finite success nor complete-delivery R proves all legal-domain inputs, unseen tasks, full-library behavior, or parameter-training gain.
source_contract.pool_limit: Task-private acceptance on the sqlparse policy-training root is not independent-confirmation material from the TextFSM pool.
source_contract.observation_limit: The saved sys.setprofile evidence identifies actual declared Python code-object calls and observed returns. sqlparse.parse returns a tuple that is not JSON-serialized in these traces; its Python type is retained. Reader-return/output equality is a finite witness, not proof by causal intervention.

member_script_early_exit_inference.mechanism_inference: The member runner uses runpy.run_path(..., run_name=__main__). unittest.main defaults to exit=True and sys.exit(0) after successful tests. The outer sandbox prints its nonce completion marker only after exec returns normally; SystemExit can terminate the process before that line, yielding zero exit status without the marker. This source chain is consistent with both saved outcomes, but no rerun is used to experimentally confirm the path.
